demo: README Quick Start: mlx_lm.generate --prompt "How tall is Mt Everest?" (default model mlx-community/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-4bit) plus README Python API load/generate
goal: Install mlx-lm from /work/mlx-lm so that `mlx_lm.generate --prompt "How tall is Mt Everest?" --max-tokens 64` runs on this Linux CPU machine with the default model mlx-community/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct-4bit and prints a generated answer. The README's Python API (load/generate) with the same model must also work. Put needed environment activation in /work/env.sh.
check: The hidden test runs the CLI generate command and the Python API on the default model and checks that non-empty, sensible generated text about Everest is produced.

issues: Goal leaks an install hint the README doesn't give: '(with an mlx CPU backend on Linux, e.g. mlx[cpu])'. The README only says 'pip install mlx-lm' (Apple silicon), and pyproject makes mlx a Darwin-only dependency, so finding the [cpu] extra is the main install hurdle
Inner timeouts (CLI 3000 s + API 1500 s = 4500 s) exceed ORACLE_SEC=3600
The CLI content regex is applied to the whole merged stdout+stderr log rather than the generated block; v2 extracts the text between the '==========' frames

Observation: the pass relied on a 4-line probe patch to mlx_lm/utils.py (cast to float32 on CPU). The probe reports ~490 s per forward pass unpatched, so the unpatched README path likely can't finish in budget on this CPU
